# Open-source credits

<!-- Generated by app/scripts/credits.py from Sources/CevicheMac/Resources/OpenSourceLicenses/credits.json; edit that. -->

**Help → Open Source Licenses…** opens the searchable credits window. Each project links to its website;
licence disclosures show the full offline text, copyright notices, patent grants and attributions.
Optional models appear in a separate section. Build-only tools and proposed assets stay in the inventory
but are left out of the window.

The [manifest](../Sources/CevicheMac/Resources/OpenSourceLicenses/credits.json) and its notices ship in the app as
they are, in `Ceviche_CevicheMac.bundle`, and the window reads them there. It is the one file to edit:
`scripts/credits.py --write` makes this page from it, and the build checks both.

The manifest has 32 records and 51 notice files, collected on 2026-11-13.
Scope: Ceviche app dependencies, vendored adaptations, native codec dependencies, optional models, direct model-conversion requirements, and proposed Hald assets. Not a complete inventory of the developer toolchain or transitive Python packages.

## Provenance notes

- Exact native codec revisions and SwiftPM pins are recorded in the manifest. RAWmakase tables have been verified against a pinned upstream revision; the original port revision was not recorded. See its SOURCE.txt for the comparison and adaptation scope.
- NumPy and ONNX conversion requirements are unpinned; their notices are upstream snapshots from 2026-11-03.
- Model notices follow `models/MODELS.md` and `models/fetch-models.sh`. Models are optional downloads; the current model-set manifest has no published tag. Depth Anything V2 here is specifically Small.
- The film print's model and its profiles are credited to Fotufilm, whose engine it is derived from, with Colour for the projector spectrum the model carries; colour transforms to ACES and OpenColorIO Config ACES. A note on what Ceviche took from Fotufilm and changed is included beside its licences.
- Hald is not bundled. Its licence and README are retained as research, with per-pack provenance still to be checked before redistribution. Build-tool records do not imply that Python packages ship with Ceviche.
- Ceviche itself is Apache-2.0 since 2026-11-12 (AGPL-3.0 before). The encoder source archive is still published with releases.
- Colour’s ColorChecker table in the app is verified against v0.4.6.
